Fitted rates, residuals and summaries of fitted models

Source: R/model-inspect.R
fit-inspection.Rd

fitted() returns the in-sample fitted death rates as an array [age, period, stratum] (NA for models without fitted values, such as the plain random walk). residuals() returns deviance residuals (default) or Pearson residuals of the death counts, assuming Poisson deaths given the fitted rates, as a long table; values far beyond 2 in absolute value point to structure that the model misses (for example cohort effects) or to overdispersion. summary() describes the model, its sources of uncertainty and the fit; mt_plot_residuals() shows the residuals as an age-period heat map.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mt_fit'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mt_fit'
residuals(object, type = c("deviance", "pearson"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'mt_fit'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

object

An mt_fit object.

...

Not used.

type

"deviance" or "pearson".

Value

fitted(): an array; residuals(): a data.table with stratum, age, period, deaths, fitted_deaths, residual; summary(): an object of class summary.mt_fit, printed.

Examples

x <- mt_example(deaths = "single")
fit <- mt_fit(lee_carter(), x)
summary(fit)
#> Lee-Carter
#>   data: 2 strata; ages 30 to 100+; periods 1990-2019
#>   model and uncertainty:
#>     log m(x,t) = a(x) + b(x) k(t), estimated by Poisson maximum likelihood
#>     (Brouhns et al. 2002; Lee and Carter 1992). k(t) follows a random walk with
#>     drift; draws include its innovations and the uncertainty of the drift. a(x)
#>     and b(x) are fixed (parameter uncertainty with bootstrapped()). Jump-off:
#>     fitted rates.
#>   fit: Poisson deviance 4105.7 on 4260 cells (0.96 per cell); 4.1% of deviance residuals beyond +/-2
head(residuals(fit))
#>    stratum    age period deaths fitted_deaths   residual
#>     <char> <char>  <num>  <num>         <num>      <num>
#> 1:  female     30   1990     84      79.27054  0.5260417
#> 2:  female     31   1990    100      88.53964  1.1929981
#> 3:  female     32   1990     93      91.57006  0.1490452
#> 4:  female     33   1990    104      99.82076  0.4154301
#> 5:  female     34   1990    105     109.53592 -0.4364418
#> 6:  female     35   1990     96     107.46697 -1.1267445
